objects.alt: A dark house with glowing windows behind an iron fence, under a full moon
Bats circle the full moon (animated)

objects.text: Your friends dared you to spend one night in the old Ashby house. The gate creaks open on its own.

objects.alt: Inside the front door: double doors bound with chains and a padlock, a grandfather clock at eleven, a coat stand

objects.text: The door slams behind you, then the chains rattle tight. The clock strikes eleven. One hour until midnight.

objects.alt: A dark hall with a doorway on the left, a portrait with red eyes, a lamp on a table and a padlocked wooden door
The lamp, now lit

objects.text: It is dark. You feel a lamp on a table. Doors lead to a study, the garden, and a cellar with a heavy lock.

objects.alt: A close-up of the portrait: a girl with dark hair and a red ribbon in a grey dress, in a gold frame with a brass name plate

objects.text: The brass plate reads: ELEANOR ASHBY, 1898–1910. The paint is cracked, but her eyes follow you.

objects.alt: A study with a full bookshelf, a desk with a candle and a drawer, and a moonlit window
The candle on the desk flickers (animated)

objects.text: A dusty desk. Something pale is tucked into the top drawer.

objects.alt: Eleanor's open diary with a red ribbon

objects.text:
October 30th, 1910.

Papa says if I am late again he will lock the door and I can sleep with the lanterns.

The lanterns sing to me from the woods. I think they know the way to somewhere better.

objects.alt: A spider web in the corner of the paper

objects.text:
If you find this, I am already gone.

I buried the cellar key by the third grave in the garden.

The ghost below fears the dark. Show it a light.

— E.

objects.alt: A moonlit garden of crooked graves behind the house, a bare tree and a small purple ghost
A rusty key in the fresh earth

objects.text: Crooked graves behind the house. A small ghost watches you from the hill.
Which grave? There are so many.
You dig up a rusty key!

objects.alt: A worn gravestone with a green light above it

objects.text:
HENRY ASHBY. Father. 1862–1911.

The second stone is worn smooth.

The third has no name, only words:

SHE FOLLOWED THE LIGHTS.

objects.alt: A stone cellar with stairs on the left and an iron door held by a golden padlock
A pale ghost floating in front of the iron door

objects.text: A pale ghost floats before the iron door. “Show me a light,” it whispers.
The ghost laughs. It is too dark to find the way out.

objects.alt: The cellar wall with the iron door swung open onto the moonlit woods, the padlock on the floor
The ghost of Henry Ashby, shrunk small by the light
Your lit lamp, held up high

objects.text: “I am Henry Ashby. I locked my daughter out, and she never came home. If you see her, tell her I am sorry.”

objects.alt: A forest road at night with green and violet lights floating above it

objects.text: The iron door opens onto a forest road. Two lights float ahead. Behind you, a whisper: “Follow the green.”

objects.alt: The forest road lost in thick fog, faint lights circling

objects.text: The violet light giggles and vanishes. You walk in circles until you find the fork again.

objects.alt: A clearing in the woods ringed by mushrooms, glowing green in the middle, fireflies all around
Eleanor, a small ghost girl in a grey dress, standing in the green light

objects.text: The green light stops and becomes a girl in a grey dress. Eleanor. “Is Papa still angry?”

objects.alt: The Ashby house at dawn, its door open and lit, gold lights drifting up the path

objects.text: Eleanor smiles for the first time in a hundred years. Her light turns gold and drifts back toward the house.

objects.alt: Sunrise over green hills, with the house far behind and a small ghost waving

objects.text: Dawn. Your friends are waiting at the gate. Nobody believes a word of your story. The end.
